uncited: The Scene Contraction Function maps an unbounded 3D scene into a bounded unit cube to facilitate efficient multiresolution grid storage and Level of Detail (LoD) computation.
No specific data structure is required for the function itself; it operates on scalar/vector types.
The implementation must support the L-infinity norm calculation.
The function applies a piecewise transformation based on the magnitude of the input position relative to the unit cube boundary (1.0).
Compute the L-infinity norm of the input position: $n = \|p\|_\infty$.
*   **LOD Factor:** The reduction from a size-2 cube to a size-1 cube introduces a factor of 2 in the LOD computation formula.
*   **LOD Behavior in Contracted Space:** In the region where $\|p\|_\infty > 1$, the computed LOD $L$ may increase with distance due to the $\log(\|p\|_\infty^4)$ term in the numerator.
This occurs because the fixed volume of a grid cell in the contracted space represents an increasingly larger volume of the original scene as distance from the center increases.
This variant defines the specific Level of Detail (LoD) formula derived from the contraction function.
*   **Increasing LOD with Distance:** As noted in the main method, the term $-4\log(\|p\|_\infty)$ in the numerator can cause $L$ to increase as $\|p\|_\infty$ grows (for $\|p\|_\infty > 1$).
This reflects the geometric property that contracted grid cells cover larger scene volumes at greater distances.
Without contraction, high-resolution grids are typically only beneficial for near-field objects.
